title: A Single Spin Switches the Steady-State Phase of an Open Quantum System
abstract: Changing a many-body system by one constituent is normally expected to produce only a vanishing correction to an intensive observable. Here we show that, above a critical dissipation imbalance, adding one spin at fixed intensive controls switches the steady state of a dissipative collective spin between a phase-averaged ring and a south-polar fixed point. Unlike previously proposed one-spin sensing through dark-state interference, parity here determines whether the Dicke ladder samples a zero of the state-dependent nonlinear-loss amplitude. The integer-spin ladder samples this zero, making Dicke states with m<0 transient; the half-integer ladder misses it and remains a single recurrent class. Exact finite-size steady states show that exponential competition between stationary weights amplifies this microscopic connectivity difference, yielding a first-order dissipative phase transition confined to the odd-N sequence. One-spin loading, with all populated spin sectors retained, confirms that rare quantum fluctuations induce the switch without postselection. Our results establish jump-operator zeros as a route for single-constituent control of steady-state phases.
summary: This paper demonstrates that adding a single spin to an open quantum system can induce a first-order phase transition, switching the steady state between two macroscopically distinct regimes. This control mechanism is fundamentally linked to the parity of the system size, which dictates whether the system samples a specific zero in the loss amplitude. The findings establish jump-operator zeros as a general route for single-constituent control over quantum steady states.
main_problem: The study investigates whether adding a single constituent spin to a many-body open quantum system can induce a macroscopic switch between distinct steady-state phases.
main_result: The system exhibits a first-order dissipative phase transition, where the steady state switches between a phase-averaged ring and a south-polar fixed point, depending on the parity of the number of spins.
method: The analysis employs steady-state calculations using the Lindblad equation, focusing on rate potentials, large-deviation theory, and analyzing parity-dependent connectivity defects in the Dicke ladder.
model_or_system: The model is an open quantum system of N spin-1/2 constituents governed by a Lindblad equation, analyzed on the Dicke ladder structure. The dynamics are controlled by a dissipation imbalance parameter, $\eta$.
key_observables: Steady-state phases (SSO ring vs. s-PFP), magnetization contrast ($\Delta m_z$), and the order parameter derived from rate potentials.
important_parameters: Dissipation imbalance ($\eta$), critical imbalance ($\eta_c$), and the parity of the total number of spins (N).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the macroscopic switch is a global large-deviation effect, not a finite-order correction, and involves analyzing the system's behavior near specific zero-current conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the macroscopic switch between even-N and odd-N steady states, the parity-dependent connectivity defect (jump zero) in the Dicke ladder, and the evolution of rate potentials and crossing times with system size.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general problem of single-constituent control, to deriving the parity-dependent connectivity defect, calculating the first-order phase transition via rate potentials, and finally analyzing the associated metastable dynamics and switching exponents.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-perturbative mechanism—using parity selection via jump-operator zeros—to control the macroscopic steady state of an open quantum system, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum dissipation and control in AMO physics.
